intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy-2 (CHN2) is caused by mutation in the gene encoding myelin protein zero (MPZ; 159440) on chromosome 1q23.3.

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy-2 (CHN2) is caused by mutation in the gene encoding myelin protein zero (MPZ).
checks.evidence_quote: the identification of a mutation in the gene (MPZ) for protein zero (P0) associated with this phenotype are described
checks.explanation: The paper links an MPZ mutation to congenital hypomyelination. CHN2 is the OMIM name for this disorder.

checks.claim: The MPZ gene is located on chromosome 1q23.3.
checks.evidence_quote: the identification of a mutation in the gene (MPZ) for protein zero (P0)
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature added to the gene name. The abstract does not state it.

paragraphs.text: Kochanski et al. (2004) described congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy (CHN) as a severe neuropathy. Smit et al. (2008) noted that onset is prenatal, neonatal or early infantile. Mandich et al. (1999) listed its features as hypotonia, distal muscle weakness, areflexia and severe slowing of nerve conduction velocities. According to Kochanski et al. (2004), sural nerve biopsy shows nonmyelinated and poorly myelinated axons and no myelin breakdown products. Mandich et al. (1999) concluded that congenital hypomyelination is allelic with less severe disorders, including Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1B (CMT1B) and Dejerine-Sottas syndrome (DSS).

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy (CHN) is a severe neuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy (CHN; MIM# 605253) is a severe neuropathy with early infancy onset
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly.

checks.claim: Onset of congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is prenatal, neonatal or early infantile.
checks.evidence_quote: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is a rare condition characterized by prenatal, neonatal or early infantile onset of hypotonia, paresis and areflexia.
checks.explanation: The abstract states the onset directly.

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is characterized by hypotonia.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by early infancy onset, distal muscle weakness, hypotonia, areflexia, and severe slowing of nerve conduction velocities
checks.explanation: The abstract lists hypotonia as a feature.

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is characterized by distal muscle weakness.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by early infancy onset, distal muscle weakness, hypotonia, areflexia, and severe slowing of nerve conduction velocities
checks.explanation: The abstract lists distal muscle weakness as a feature.

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is characterized by areflexia.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by early infancy onset, distal muscle weakness, hypotonia, areflexia, and severe slowing of nerve conduction velocities
checks.explanation: The abstract lists areflexia as a feature.

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is characterized by severe slowing of nerve conduction velocities.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by early infancy onset, distal muscle weakness, hypotonia, areflexia, and severe slowing of nerve conduction velocities
checks.explanation: The abstract lists severe slowing of nerve conduction velocities as a feature.

checks.claim: In congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy, sural nerve biopsy shows nonmyelinated and poorly myelinated axons.
checks.evidence_quote: Sural nerve biopsy shows a characteristic picture of nonmyelinated and poorly myelinated axons with basal lamina onion bulbs and lack of myelin breakdown products.
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly.

checks.claim: In congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy, sural nerve biopsy shows no myelin breakdown products.
checks.evidence_quote: Sural nerve biopsy shows a characteristic picture of nonmyelinated and poorly myelinated axons with basal lamina onion bulbs and lack of myelin breakdown products.
checks.explanation: "Lack of myelin breakdown products" means the same as "no myelin breakdown products."

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelination is allelic with less severe disorders, including Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1B (CMT1B) and Dejerine-Sottas syndrome (DSS).
checks.evidence_quote: quite distinct from those of the more frequent Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 1B disease (CMT1B) or Dejerine-Sottas syndrome (DSS) confirms that CH is allelic with other disorders characterized by a less severe phenotype
checks.explanation: The abstract concludes that CH is allelic with milder disorders and names CMT1B and DSS in the same sentence. The claim combines these two parts.

paragraphs.text: Kochanski et al. (2004) noted that CHN is inherited as an autosomal dominant or recessive trait. Mandich et al. (1999) reported a de novo MPZ mutation in a patient with congenital hypomyelination.

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is inherited as an autosomal dominant or autosomal recessive trait.
checks.evidence_quote: inherited as an autosomal dominant or recessive trait
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly.

checks.claim: A patient with congenital hypomyelination carried a de novo MPZ mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: This "de novo" mutation in a patient presenting with clinical features quite distinct from those
checks.explanation: The abstract states the patient's MPZ mutation was de novo.

paragraphs.text: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is genetically heterogeneous. Kochanski et al. (2004) noted that mutations in several genes have been found in patients with CHN, including the EGR2 gene.

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: Several mutations in the MTMR2, PMP22, EGR2, and MPZ genes have been found in patients with CHN.
checks.explanation: Mutations in four different genes cause CHN, so the disorder is genetically heterogeneous. The paper does not use that word, but the conclusion follows directly.

checks.claim: Mutations in several genes, including the EGR2 gene, have been found in patients with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Several mutations in the MTMR2, PMP22, EGR2, and MPZ genes have been found in patients with CHN.
checks.explanation: The abstract names EGR2 among several genes with mutations found in CHN patients.

paragraphs.text: Warner et al. (1996) studied patients with inherited peripheral neuropathies and identified mutations in the MPZ gene in patients with CMT1B, DSS, or congenital hypomyelination (CH). They suggested that these disorders may not be distinct pathophysiologic entities. Instead, they proposed that the disorders represent a spectrum of related myelinopathies.

checks.claim: Warner et al. (1996) studied patients with inherited peripheral neuropathies.
checks.evidence_quote: Hereditary demyelinating peripheral neuropathies consist of a heterogeneous group of genetic disorders
checks.explanation: The abstract describes studying patients with hereditary demyelinating peripheral neuropathies.

checks.claim: Mutations in the MPZ gene were found in patients with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1B (CMT1B).
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified five novel mutations in the myelin protein zero (MPZ) gene, encoding the major structural protein (P0) of peripheral nerve myelin, in patients with either CMT1B, DSS, or CH.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that MPZ mutations were found in CMT1B patients.

checks.claim: Mutations in the MPZ gene were found in patients with Dejerine-Sottas syndrome (DSS).
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified five novel mutations in the myelin protein zero (MPZ) gene, encoding the major structural protein (P0) of peripheral nerve myelin, in patients with either CMT1B, DSS, or CH.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that MPZ mutations were found in DSS patients.

checks.claim: Mutations in the MPZ gene were found in patients with congenital hypomyelination (CH).
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified five novel mutations in the myelin protein zero (MPZ) gene, encoding the major structural protein (P0) of peripheral nerve myelin, in patients with either CMT1B, DSS, or CH.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that MPZ mutations were found in CH patients.

checks.claim: CMT1B, DSS and congenital hypomyelination may not be distinct pathophysiologic entities.
checks.evidence_quote: This finding suggests that these disorders may not be distinct pathophysiologic entities
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: CMT1B, DSS and congenital hypomyelination may represent a spectrum of related myelinopathies.
checks.evidence_quote: but rather represent a spectrum of related "myelinopathies" due to an underlying defect in myelination.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Mandich et al. (1999) identified a de novo MPZ mutation in a patient with congenital hypomyelination. They concluded that CH is allelic with disorders that have a less severe phenotype, such as CMT1B and DSS.

checks.claim: A de novo MPZ mutation was found in a patient with congenital hypomyelination.
checks.evidence_quote: This "de novo" mutation in a patient presenting with clinical features quite distinct from those
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a de novo MPZ mutation in a patient with CH.

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelination is allelic with disorders that have a less severe phenotype, such as CMT1B and DSS.
checks.evidence_quote: quite distinct from those of the more frequent Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 1B disease (CMT1B) or Dejerine-Sottas syndrome (DSS) confirms that CH is allelic with other disorders characterized by a less severe phenotype
checks.explanation: The abstract supports the conclusion and mentions CMT1B and DSS in the same sentence. The claim combines these two parts.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Prenatal, neonatal or early infantile onset
Severe slowing of nerve conduction velocities
Nonmyelinated and poorly myelinated axons on sural nerve biopsy
